subtopics.title: The Energy Engine and Global Circulation

questions.question: The tropics run an energy surplus and the poles a deficit because:
options: The sun's rays strike the tropics almost vertically, concentrated after a short passage through the atmosphere, while polar rays arrive at a shallow angle, spread thin after a long slanting journey
The tropics contain more ocean than the poles
The poles face away from the sun all year round
Volcanic heat warms the tropics from below

questions.question: The chain that converts temperature into wind runs:
options: Wind stirs the air, which changes pressure, which changes temperature
Warm air rises leaving surface low pressure, cold air sinks stacking high pressure, and wind is air draining from high toward low
High pressure heats the air, which then rises as wind
Wind is caused only by the earth's rotation

questions.question: In the Hadley cell, air:
options: Sinks at the equator and rises at 30 degrees
Circulates only above the poles
Rises at the equator, streams poleward aloft, subsides near 30 degrees, and returns as the trade winds
Flows poleward along the surface and returns aloft

questions.question: The Coriolis force explains why:
options: Winds always blow from the poles to the equator
The pressure belts never migrate
Air stops moving at the equator
Southern-hemisphere winds bend left — turning honest north-south flows into south-east trades and south-westerly Cape gales

questions.question: The ITCZ delivers southern Africa's wet season because:
options: It is the rising seam where the two hemispheres' trade winds collide, and it migrates south with the overhead sun in our summer
It blocks all moisture from reaching the interior
It is a band of sinking, drying air
It only ever affects the northern hemisphere

questions.question: The Highveld's dry, frosty winter weather is locked in by:
options: The Agulhas current cooling the plateau
The Kalahari High parked over the interior, whose subsiding air seals the plateau under cloudless, windless conditions
The ITCZ sitting directly overhead
Permanent westerly storms over Gauteng

questions.question: The four-stage drought ladder runs:
options: Agricultural, meteorological, socio-economic, hydrological
Socio-economic first, then rainfall shortfall last
Meteorological shortfall, then hydrological drawdown of rivers and dams, then agricultural failure of soil moisture, then socio-economic impacts on livelihoods
Hydrological, agricultural, meteorological, socio-economic

questions.question: Drought differs from desertification in that:
options: Drought is permanent while desertification passes quickly
Both are purely natural and identical in cause
Desertification is caused only by El Niño
Drought is a temporary rainfall shortfall, while desertification is long-term, mostly human-caused degradation of dryland until it behaves like desert

subtopics.title: Reading Rock into Landscape — Horizontal, Inclined and Massive

questions.question: The shrinking sequence carved from flat Karoo strata runs:
options: Plateau, then mesa, then butte, then conical hill — driven by differential erosion under a dolerite cap
Conical hill, then butte, then mesa, then plateau
Cuesta, then hogsback, then tor, then dome
Butte, then plateau, then cone, then mesa

questions.question: A mesa becomes a butte when:
options: Its cap rock thickens over time
Continued slope retreat leaves the flat-topped hill higher than its narrow summit is wide
The dolerite cap folds into a ridge
Rivers deposit sediment on its summit

questions.question: Ranked by dip angle, the tilted-strata ridges are:
options: Hogsback gentlest, cuesta steepest
All three form at exactly 25 degrees
Cuesta at gentle dip, homoclinal ridge at moderate dip, hogsback where strata stand near-vertical — the steeper the tilt, the more equal the slopes
Homoclinal ridges only form in flat strata

questions.question: Granite landscapes stay rounded because:
options: Granite is too soft to hold a cliff
Layering in granite forms natural steps
Glaciers polished all granite smooth
Massive unlayered granite exfoliates — shedding curved onion-skin shells as pressure release expands the surface — while rotted joint blocks emerge as stacked tors

subtopics.title: Slopes, Mass Movement and the Map

questions.question: Recited downhill, the four slope elements are:
options: Crest, cliff or free face, talus slope, pediment
Pediment, talus, cliff, crest
Scarp, dip, poort, dome
Crest, pediment, cliff, talus

questions.question: Soil creep is identified in the field by:
options: Fresh crescent-shaped scars at a slope's head
Fence posts leaning downhill, tilted poles and tree trunks curved at the base
Rivers of liquid mud in the valleys
Boulders bouncing from the free face

questions.question: A slump differs from a landslide because a slump:
options: Moves faster than any other mass movement
Only occurs on perfectly dry slopes
Rotates backward along a curved surface as it drops, leaving a crescent scar, while a landslide shears along a straight plane
Involves only single falling blocks

questions.question: A rise of one hundred metres across two thousand metres of ground gives a gradient of:
options: One in two hundred
One in ten
One in one hundred
One in twenty

subtopics.title: Three Conveyor Belts and a Merry-Go-Round

questions.question: The world's great deserts sit near 30 degrees because:
options: Air that rose at the equator descends there — and sinking air is dry air that dissolves cloud instead of building it
The oceans are furthest away at that latitude
The Coriolis force is strongest there
Volcanoes heat the crust along that belt

questions.question: The merry-go-round picture explains Coriolis because:
options: Merry-go-rounds generate their own wind
A ball rolled across a turning platform runs true through space, yet curves when watched from the rotating seat — just as winds curve over the turning earth
The earth speeds up and slows down like a ride
Winds only blow while the earth accelerates

questions.question: Johannesburg and Cape Town have opposite rain seasons because:
options: The two cities sit in different hemispheres
Cape Town's mountains block all summer rain
In summer the ITCZ dips south to drench the interior while in winter the Kalahari High dries the plateau and the displaced westerlies drag fronts across the Cape
The Agulhas current reverses direction seasonally

subtopics.title: The Layer Cake, the Tilted Books and the Rising Loaf

questions.question: In the rained-on cake, the chocolate lid stands for:
options: The resistant dolerite cap rock protecting the softer shale beneath
The soft shale that erodes fastest
The rivers that cut the valleys
The soil profile above the bedrock

questions.question: The tilted-books hook — the steeper the tilt, the more equal the slopes — orders the ridges as:
options: Hogsback, homoclinal ridge, cuesta as tilt increases
Cuesta at gentle tilt, homoclinal ridge at moderate tilt, hogsback when the books stand nearly upright
All three ridges at the same angle
Cuesta steepest, hogsback gentlest

questions.question: Granite behaves like a loaf fresh from the tin because:
options: It doubles in size when exposed to air
It burns dark on its upper surface
Released from confining pressure, its surface expands and flakes off in curved crusts — exfoliation, which keeps the hills domed
It absorbs rainwater like fresh bread

questions.question: Tors form when:
options: Volcanoes stack lava blocks above the surface
Rivers pile boulders at their mouths
Glaciers drop balanced rocks as they melt
Groundwater rots the corners off jointed granite blocks underground, and erosion sweeps the grit away leaving rounded cores stacked in piles

subtopics.title: One Walk Down the Hillside — Slopes, Slides and the Exam

questions.question: On the walk downhill, the talus is recognised because:
options: It is sharp, loose rubble resting at the steepest angle loose rock can hold — kick a stone and it clatters, slides and stops
It is the rounded shoulder at the summit
It is the bare vertical rock face
It is the gentle concave run-out to the flats

questions.question: The Merriespruit disaster illustrates that:
options: Rockfall is the deadliest mass movement
Saturated fluid mud is lethal at speed — a failed tailings dam sent a mudflow through part of a town
Soil creep can bury buildings overnight
Slumps only occur on natural slopes

questions.question: On the contour map, a cuesta signs its name by:
options: Perfectly circular, evenly spaced rings
A blank area with no contours at all
Asymmetry — lines jammed together on the scarp flank and strolling far apart down the dip slope
Contours that cross one another repeatedly

questions.question: Intervisibility between two stations is settled by asking:
options: Whether the two points share the same contour line
Whether the map's scale is larger than one in fifty thousand
Whether a river flows between the points
Whether a convex bulge lifts between the two points and blocks the sight line
